results.summary_before: This design implements a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor for RISC-V processors, using SPI to receive branch addresses and ground truth directions. It is tested with CocoTB and a functional simulation that parses Spike execution logs, and it requires external hardware to drive and read its pins. Notable features include latch-based memory from a third-party repository and detailed documentation with waveforms. The design is not single-cycle due to memory constraints and includes debug outputs for monitoring internal state.
results.summary: This design implements a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor that reads the lower 8 bits of a branch instruction address and its ground truth direction over basic SPI. It uses latch-based memory from a third-party repository and is not single-cycle due to memory architecture constraints. It is tested with CocoTB and a C++ functional simulation that parses Spike execution logs of a RISC-V reference program. The design exposes debug outputs for monitoring internal state and requires external hardware to drive and read its pins.

results.summary_before: This design implements a tiny FABulous FPGA fabric with 128 LUT4+FF logic cells arranged in an 8x4 tile grid, including carry chains and global buffers. The I/O mimics the Tiny Tapeout interface, allowing user designs to be synthesized with Yosys and nextpnr, then loaded via a bitbang interface using ui[0] and ui[1] while reset is held low. The bitstream is uploaded while rst_n is asserted, and after configuration, the user design runs on the fabric. This is a notable open-source FPGA fabric intended for use as a reconfigurable target for small digital designs, with no external hardware required.

results.summary_before: This design computes the Collatz sequence for a large integer input, returning the orbit length and an indicator of the maximum value reached. The input number is uploaded byte-by-byte into a 144-bit register via an address bus, and the computation is started with a pin; the busy indicator is polled until completion, after which the results are read back in 16-bit chunks. The design is intended for brute-force searching of path records, and the documentation explains the state machine and I/O protocol in detail. No external hardware is required beyond the chip itself.
